key_insight: Concordat makes action rules runtime-enforced finite-state protocols rather than relying on an LLM agent to obey prompt instructions.
engineering_relevance: Its Python interface helps protect consequential workflows by blocking illegal tool calls before side effects and reserving human decisions for humans.
method: Expose only tools permitted in the current protocol state and reject out-of-protocol calls.
Check protocols at definition time and reject subclasses that could bypass inherited constraints.
Charge and split token and tool-call budgets linearly across agent handoffs.
evidence_signal: On tau-bench’s 50 airline tasks with simulated customer pressure, Concordat had zero confirmation violations versus 13/50 GPT-4.1 tasks and 29/128 Claude Haiku 5.5 task-runs for the standard agent, with no significant task-success difference.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the reported airline benchmark; deployment still requires correctly specified protocols covering consequential actions.
paper_title: Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents
